name: Maher 2011
aliases: LSC versus total vaginal mesh for vault prolapse
question: Does laparoscopic sacral colpopexy improve two-year anatomic success compared with total transvaginal mesh repair for symptomatic vault prolapse?

design.blinding: Patients and surgeons unmasked; independent reviewers masked after the 6-week visit
design.population: Women with symptomatic post-hysterectomy vaginal vault prolapse of POP-Q stage 2 or higher were randomized at a Brisbane tertiary urogynecology unit.

verdictNote: Two-year objective success favored laparoscopy; Prolift recipients underwent more surgery-related reoperations.
takeaway: Laparoscopic sacral colpopexy yielded higher two-year objective anatomic success than total transvaginal Gynecare Prolift mesh repair for symptomatic vault prolapse (41/53 versus 23/55; OR 4.75, 95% CI 2.06–10.98); surgery-related reoperation affected 3/53 versus 12/55.

reports.label: Two-year randomized report
reports.citation: Maher CF, Feiner B, DeCuyper EM, et al. "Laparoscopic sacral colpopexy versus total vaginal mesh for vaginal vault prolapse: a randomized trial." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;204(4):360.e1-360.e7. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2010.11.016
reports.followUp: Mean 2-year assessment; all 108 women completed at least 6 months

results.endpoint: Objective anatomic success at all vaginal sites
results.measure: POP-Q stage 0 or 1 at Aa, Ba, C, Bp and Ap at mean 2 years
results.note: Intention-to-treat comparison; prespecified two-sided alpha 0.05. The article prints 43% for 23/55, although that fraction rounds to 42%.

results.measure: Mean score on 0–100 patient-rated satisfaction scale at mean 2 years; mean difference
results.note: Between-arm mean difference favors laparoscopic sacral colpopexy.

results.endpoint: Pelvic-floor symptoms and quality of life
results.measure: Within-arm change on APFQ and P-QoL questionnaires
results.note: No significant between-arm difference in pre-to-postoperative score changes was detected.

harms.label: Surgery-related reoperation
harms.note: Three versus 15 reoperations in three versus 12 women (P=0.006; OR for TVM versus LSC 4.65, 95% CI 1.23–17.57). The article prints 5% for 3/53, although that fraction rounds to 6%.

harms.label: Vaginal mesh erosion
harms.note: P=0.07; two asymptomatic women in the vaginal mesh arm declined correction.

harms.label: Intraoperative injury and conversion
harms.note: Both injuries were repaired intraoperatively; after enterotomy, the assigned laparoscopic procedure was converted to vaginal mesh repair and analyzed in the laparoscopic arm.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection and transfusion
harms.note: One vaginal mesh patient was readmitted with an infected pelvic hematoma treated with intravenous antibiotics.

delivery.label: Surgeon experience
delivery.value: The consultant urogynecologist and fellow had each completed at least 30 laparoscopic and vaginal prolapse mesh operations before trial surgery.

delivery.label: Laparoscopic repair
delivery.value: Self-fashioned large-pore polypropylene Y mesh sutured to both vaginal walls with polydioxanone, tacked to the sacral promontory, and covered by peritoneum.

delivery.label: Vaginal repair
delivery.value: Total Gynecare Prolift kit with absorbable fixation of distal anterior and posterior tails to vaginal fascia; TVT-O added for overt or occult stress incontinence.

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures
delivery.note: Concomitant operations followed compartment defects and stress-incontinence status.

delivery.label: Median operating time, blood loss and inpatient stay
delivery.note: Operating time P<0.001; blood loss P=0.004; inpatient stay P=0.01.

delivery.label: Return to normal activity
delivery.note: Mean difference −5.34 days (95% CI −8.36 to −2.32); the equal medians conceal the distributional difference.

relations.note: Used that trial's open sacral colpopexy technique and success estimate to plan the laparoscopic arm.
